items.author: ray.kessler
items.body: Reminder all: haul-out weekend is Nov 21-22 at the yard on Willoughby Bay. Sign-up sheet is pinned. If you're staying in the water this winter, you're on your own for winterizing, but the usual suspects in #maintenance are good about helping.

items.author: marcy.tillotson
items.body: Frostbite series starts Dec 6 if the weather cooperates. Need two more boats on the line or we fold it into the spring. Walt, are you in with Pelican Rest?

items.author: dana.okoye
items.body: Okay, first winter as a boat owner and I am a little out of my depth. Bought Sea Wren (2003 Catalina 30, Yanmar 3GM30F) in June, keeping her in the water at our slips. The yard quoted me $465 to winterize the engine and water system. Is this something I can realistically do myself in an afternoon? I've changed the oil once with Hector's help. What do I need, what order, and what can actually go wrong if I mess it up? Not trying to cheap out, I just want to understand my own boat.

items.author: hector.ruiz
items.body: Totally doable. I just run a jug of the green automotive stuff through mine every year, never had a problem. Takes 20 min. Don't overthink it.

items.author: bev.sandoval
items.body: Dana you can absolutely do it. Walt walked me through mine two years ago, he's got the checklist in his head. @walt.brennan ?

items.author: gus.pereira
items.body: Anyone have a spare 1-1/4" hose clamp for the cockpit drain? Mine rotted through. Will trade beer.

items.author: ray.kessler
items.body: Walt, keep this between us till the board meets on the 17th. Dana's slip account is $1,140 behind, three months now. Treasurer wants to send a non-renewal letter. I'd rather someone talk to her quietly first. Don't raise it in the channels.
